text: Do you have a family history of dementia or psychiatric disorders, and have you noticed any involuntary jerking movements in your limbs or face? I also need to ask if you have experienced any loss of coordination or balance issues recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of suicide and your symptoms, I need to rule out Wilson's disease, so I will request liver function tests and ceruloplasmin levels. Could you also describe if the involuntary movements are more like rapid, jerky motions or a slow, writhing quality? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests, Ceruloplasmin

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative liver tests, I need to rule out other metabolic causes, so I will request a copper study and check for Wilson's disease markers. Have you noticed any tremors in your hands or difficulty with fine motor tasks, and do the involuntary movements worsen with stress? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Copper, Urine_Copper

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal copper studies effectively rule out Wilson's disease, so we must look elsewhere. Given the combination of psychiatric symptoms, cognitive decline, and choreiform movements with a family history of suicide, I suspect Huntington's disease. I will order a genetic test for the HTT gene expansion and request brain imaging to look for caudate nucleus atrophy. REQUEST TEST: Genetic_Test_Huntington, Brain_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Genetic Testing: Positive for the huntingtin (HTT) gene mutation. Brain MRI: Atrophy of the caudate nuclei with ex vacuo dilatation of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles.

speaker: Doctor
text: The genetic testing confirms a positive result for the huntingtin gene mutation, and the MRI shows characteristic caudate atrophy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Huntington's Disease
